headings.title: Introduction to Stock Holding Conventions
headings.content: Stock holding conventions refer to the standardized systems, rules, and practices used to manage healthcare supplies within a clinical facility. In Nigerian hospitals, ranging from primary healthcare centres to large tertiary teaching hospitals, maintaining an optimal inventory of drugs and medical consumables is vital for daily operations. Without structured conventions, facilities risk running out of life-saving commodities or accumulating vast stores of expired products that drain precious financial resources. These conventions bridge the gap between clinical demand and supply chain logistics, ensuring that materials are accounted for, properly stored, and readily available at the bedside.

headings.title: Purpose and Importance of Inventory Control
headings.content: Inventory control directly impacts patient safety, institutional financial health, and workflow efficiency. When nurses participate in accurate stock monitoring, they prevent critical shortages of basic items like cotton wool, syringes, and emergency medications. Effective control measures also minimize shrinkage—losses due to theft, damage, or misplacement. In many public health facilities across West Africa, stock discrepancies undermine patient trust and delay urgent interventions. Maintaining rigorous oversight guarantees that every item entering the ward is accounted for from delivery to eventual clinical administration.

headings.title: Classification of Medical and Surgical Supplies
headings.content:
Medical inventory must be categorized logically to streamline storage, access, and auditing. Common classifications include:

- **Consumables**: Single-use items such as gauze, syringes, infusion sets, and examination gloves.
- **Pharmaceuticals**: Drugs categorized by therapeutic class, emergency status, or controlled access.
- **Durables**: Reusable equipment like stainless steel instrument trays, kidney dishes, and blood pressure cuffs.
- **Surgical Implants**: Specialized items requiring strict batch tracking, such as orthopedic pins or mesh.

headings.title: Key Principles: FIFO, LIFO, and Expiry Tracking
headings.content:
Stock rotation principles govern the order in which items are selected from storage for clinical use.

- **FIFO (First-In, First-Out)**: Stock received earliest is used first. This remains the absolute gold standard for pharmaceuticals and perishables in nursing practice to prevent expiration.
- **LIFO (Last-In, First-Out)**: Stock received most recently is used first. This is rarely used in healthcare except for non-perishable bulk commodities with no degradation risk.
- **FEFO (First-Expired, First-Out)**: Items with the nearest expiration date are dispatched first, regardless of when they arrived on the shelf.

Regularly checking expiry dates prevents the dangerous practice of administering degraded medications to vulnerable patients.

headings.title: Stock Levels: Minimum, Maximum, and Reorder Points
headings.content: Understanding threshold levels prevents both unexpected stockouts and overstocking. The **minimum stock level** (or buffer stock) is the safety threshold below which stock should never fall during normal operations. The **reorder point** is the specific inventory level that triggers the generation of a new requisition order, calculated by factoring in the lead time required for delivery. The **maximum stock level** represents the upper ceiling of inventory a ward can hold without risking wastage, clutter, or exceeding storage capacity.

headings.title: Storage Conditions and Maintenance of Stock Integrity
headings.content: Medical supplies degrade rapidly if exposed to unfavorable environmental factors. Temperature control is paramount, particularly in tropical climates like Nigeria, where ambient heat can destroy thermolabile drugs such as vaccines, insulin, and oxytocin. Storage rooms must remain dry, well-ventilated, and protected from direct sunlight. Supplies must never be placed directly on the floor; pallets or metal shelving units keep items elevated and safe from dampness or pest contamination. Regular checks of refrigerator logs ensure cold chain integrity remains unbroken.

headings.title: Auditing, Stock-Taking, and Record Keeping Procedures
headings.content: Routine physical stock-taking verifies that recorded inventory numbers match actual physical counts on ward shelves. Audits expose discrepancies, deter pilferage, and highlight consumption trends. Nurses maintain bin cards, stock ledgers, and digital logs to document every item received, issued, or discarded. Accurate documentation forms the backbone of reliable healthcare logistics, ensuring accountability during shift handovers and external administrative inspections.

headings.title: Managing Waste, Discrepancies, and Expired Items
headings.content: When audits reveal expired goods or damaged consumables, formal disposal procedures must be followed. Expired medications cannot simply be tossed into ordinary ward dustbins due to environmental hazards and the risk of scavenging. Instead, they require segregation, formal documentation of write-offs, and transfer to pharmacy or waste management units for incineration or safe destruction. Unresolved discrepancies between stock ledgers and physical counts must be investigated promptly to maintain institutional accountability.
